exposures.supporting_excerpt: An increased risk was observed with higher intake of processed foods (OR 1.29, 95%CI 1.05-1.59; highest vs. lowest quartile), but not with consumption of ultra-processed food and drinks. The associations with unprocessed/minimally processed foods and processed foods were slightly more pronounced for high-grade cancers (ORs 0.80 and 1.33, respectively).
exposures.reason: Ultra-processed food and drinks are discussed only for overall prostate cancer. The high-grade analysis explicitly concerns unprocessed/minimally processed foods and processed foods, so it cannot be transferred to ultra-processed food intake.
